title: Field guide: customer choices during inference degradations
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a compact field guide intended for Customer Success and customer liaisons to use while drafting short status updates and post-incident customer summaries when inference quality or latency degrades. Goal: empower customers to choose the recovery path that best fits their needs, with clear verification steps and short copied text they can paste into their ops channels or support tickets.

Quick TL;DR (one-sentence for status page):
- We observed degraded inference quality/latency in <region/team> starting ~2028-10-07 16:12 UTC. We routed traffic to fallback capacity and rolled a prioritized remediation plan; some tenants may experience elevated latency or truncated streams while we validate results.

When to use this doc:
- Short customer status fragments (status page, support threads)
- Post-incident customer summary (concise one-pager)
- When customers ask: "What can I do?" or "Do I need to replay requests?"

Decision matrix for customers (high level):
- Option A — Continue (monitor, no action): good when outputs are usable and business impact is low. Choose if: majority of responses are coherent, latency within 2x baseline, and no data-loss risk.
- Option B — Switch to a compatible model variant: good when you prefer predictable latency over best-in-class sampling. Choose if: you rely on fast, consistent responses and can accept minor quality differences.
- Option C — Replay after fix: good when output integrity is essential (billing, legal text). Choose if: you need exact outputs and can accept temporary reprocessing cost.
- Option D — Throttle/backoff or queue requests: good for bulk batch jobs or non-interactive work during remediation window.

Customer-facing snippets (copy/paste):
- Status page short (50–80 chars): "Partial inference degradation in US-west; reduced throughput and elevated latency while we validate fallback."
- Support thread opener: "We observed inconsistent outputs and higher latency between 2028-10-07 16:12–18:45 UTC. Our platform moved traffic to a fallback model and applied a conservative cache flush; please see recommended customer choices below and tell us which you prefer."
- Replay consent request: "We can replay affected requests for you — this will reprocess outputs with the validated model. Confirm with \"replay:yes\" and we’ll provide a verification bundle."

Verification checklist for customers (short tests to decide):
- Spot-check 10 recent requests used during the window. Are outputs acceptable? (yes/no)
- Compare avg latency on a small synthetic set (5 requests) against baseline. If >2x baseline, consider variant/switch.
- If structured outputs/truncation occurred, request a replay and ask for checksum/verification tokens post-replay.

Operator notes for support reps (how to present options):
- Step 1: confirm tenant impact (query internal incident view). Attach timestamps + example request IDs.
- Step 2: offer 2 clear choices (A) continue + monitoring (B) immediate switch-to-variant or (C) opt-in replay. Keep language simple.
- Step 3: if customer selects replay, open a ticket to eng-runbook with tag "replay-consent" and include SLA window and expected data volume.

Replay process (customer-facing summary):
- What we do: re-run affected requests through validated model variant, produce new outputs, keep original outputs in evidence bundle.
- Expected timeline: small batches (<= 10k requests) — 24–72 hrs depending on queue.
- Cost model: replaying is billable at published inference rates; for verified incidents we will evaluate partial credits — see SLA note.

Fallback / model-switch guidance (for product teams):
- Suggest customers move to model family X-compact (lower-context, quantized) if latency matters more than subtle generation quality.
- Recommend model family Y-stable for high-integrity structured outputs.
- Provide an example API snippet customers can paste to their devs: 
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" 
    -d '{ "model": "y-stable-1.1", "input": "<sample>" }' 

Evidence and verification artifacts we provide to customers after option selection:
- Timestamped sample responses (original vs replayed) 
- Per-request latency histograms for the affected interval 
- Hash list (SHA256) of payloads processed and the replayed outputs for customer-side verification

Short postmortem summary template for customers (one pager):
- Incident window: start / end (UTC)
- Impact: affected regions, % of requests, example customer-visible failures (e.g., truncation, incoherent tokens)
- Root cause (plain language): brief explanation of what failed (e.g., cache staleness + kernel mismatch on compiled runtime)
- Mitigation enacted: traffic routing, model fallback, cache invalidation, hotfix deploys
- Customer choices offered and counts: continue/variant/replay/throttle (how many customers chose each)
- Verification evidence: link to artifact bundle and instructions for reconciliation
- Next steps and commitments: timeline for followups, engineering changes, and SLA credit evaluation

Unresolved questions / TODOs (internal):
- Decide exact wording for statuspage up/down vs degraded (product wants precise thresholds).
- Confirm replay cost credit policy for incidents that impact >20% of a tenant’s requests. (finance sign-off needed)
- Add a short interactive statusflow (choice board) to the statuspage for enterprise tenants — is engineering available?

Handy snippets for engineers to include in customer emails:
- "We validated corrected outputs across a representative sample and held baseline performance within target for the replayed set. See the verification bundle attached."
- "If you prefer, we will pause any automatic billing for replayed requests until you confirm reconciliation. Reply with \"pause-billing\" to request this."

Notes to self (tone + voice):
- Keep language non-technical but precise; customers prefer explicit numbers and timelines. 
- Avoid blame wording (e.g., "we failed") — use "we observed" and "we remediated".
- Make the customer feel in control: present clear binary choices with consequences.

Appendix: quick checklist for publishing a statuspage update (operator):
1) Single-sentence summary + region list
2) Outage window and current status (mitigating / resolved / monitoring)
3) Action customers can take (copy one of the snippets above)
4) Link to evidence bundle (if released) and reply channel for opt-ins
5) ETA for next update (do not promise hard times unless verified)

End of draft.

Notes: keep short, iterative — this is intentionally terse. Use for T+0 and postmortem drafts.
